title: Testing Quality
description: Can design tests and quality gates that fail for a real risk and stay green for intended behavior — and can choose which layer would have caught a given miss.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can add characterization tests that pin existing behavior — including an edge case and an invalid input — and name one surprising result without changing the code — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can attach a failing automated case to a reproduced defect, then add a regression test that would fail if the bug returned, and run the suite with one documented command.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently write a risk-to-layer test strategy, implement tests at more than one layer, and show a deliberate failure that only that layer would catch.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a flaky, weakly asserted or contract-breaking suite, name the nondeterminism or surviving mutant, and fix the cause rather than retrying or raising coverage alone.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's suite or quality gate, name a test that is toil or vanity, and teach when a unit test is the wrong layer on a system they did not write.
